sections.overview: The Galapagos croaker is a small marine drum in the croaker family, Sciaenidae. It is known from the Galapagos Islands and nearby Cocos Island in the eastern Pacific.
sections.identification: It has a short, deep, laterally compressed body and a conspicuously large eye. Its jaws bear rows of teeth but lack enlarged front canines; the lateral line continues to the tail.
sections.habitat: It is a tropical, reef-associated fish reported from shallow water, at about 3–30 m depth. It occurs around rocky slopes and reefs in the eastern Pacific islands.
sections.diet: FishBase reports that it feeds mainly on zooplankton.
sections.behavior: It is often observed in schools or loose aggregations above rocky, algae-covered bottoms.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific reproductive details were not available in the sources reviewed for this profile.
sections.ecology: Its zooplankton diet and schooling habit place it in shallow reef food webs. Records are concentrated around oceanic islands rather than continental shores.
sections.conservation: FishBase and the Galapagos database report Least Concern in 2022, but the Smithsonian species page gives Vulnerable, so the conflict should be checked against the Red List assessment itself.
